claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a 17-year-old son, Alex, who lives with me. He's still in sixth form doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful context. Alex sounds like he would potentially qualify since he's 17 and still in approved education (A-levels in sixth form).

Before I can give you a full assessment, I need to gather a bit more information about your situation:

**Are you currently living in the UK, and is Alex living with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I live in the UK and Alex lives here with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's an important requirement met.

Now I need to ask about your immigration status, as this can affect eligibility:

**Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a British citizen/have indefinite leave to remain in the UK? Or, if you have pre-settled status, could you tell me a bit about your current circumstances (for example, are you working, studying, or claiming any benefits)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, so that shouldn't be a problem.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That simplifies things considerably. As a British citizen, you have the right to reside in the UK, which is a key requirement.

Now let me ask about your household circumstances:

**Are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there anyone else (such as Alex's other parent or another family member) who might also be claiming or considering claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's nobody else claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. That's important to confirm since only one person can get Child Benefit for a child.

Now, just to ensure I have the complete picture of your family situation:

**Do you have any other children (under 16, or aged 16-19 in approved education or training) that you're responsible for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me, let me summarize your situation:
- You're a British citizen living in the UK
- Alex is your 17-year-old son who lives with you
- He's in sixth form studying A-levels (approved education)
- You're the only person claiming Child Benefit for him

Let me now provide you with my eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- ✓ You're a British citizen living in the UK
- ✓ You live with Alex and are responsible for him
- ✓ Alex is 17 and in approved education (sixth form A-levels)
- ✓ Only you are claiming for him

Since Alex is still in approved education and under 20, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for him. The payments will continue as long as he remains in approved education or training.

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit or need help with making a claim, feel free to ask!
